pappus.name: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus.role: Alexandrian geometer & author of the Synagoge (Mathematical Collection)
pappus.summary: Last great synthetic geometer of Greek antiquity; compiled the eight-book Synagoge preserving and extending the Treasury of Analysis, projective cross-ratio and hexagon theorems, arbelos circle chains, honeycomb isoperimetry, and Alexandrian mechanics.

pandrosion.name: Pandrosion of Alexandria
pandrosion.role: Alexandrian woman mathematician & teacher of geometry, dedicatee of Synagoge Book III
pandrosion.summary: Addressed by Pappus at the opening of Book III (ὦ κρατίστη Πανδροσίων, restored by Hultsch from feminine vocative manuscript readings where Commandino had assumed masculine); taught advanced solid-problem geometry in fourth-century Alexandria.

megethius.name: Megethius
megethius.role: Dedicatee of Synagoge Book V (On Isoperimetric Figures)
megethius.summary: Addressed by Pappus in the celebrated Preface on the geometrical forethought of bees and plane/solid isoperimetry opening Book V.

hermodorus.name: Hermodorus
hermodorus.role: Son of Pappus & dedicatee of Synagoge Books VII and VIII
hermodorus.summary: Pappus's son ('ὦ τέκνον Ἑρμόδωρε'), for whose advanced mathematical studies Pappus composed both Book VII (Treasury of Analysis) and Book VIII (Mechanics).

hierius.name: Hierius
hierius.role: Philosopher & friend of Pappus mentioned in Book III
hierius.summary: Philosophical colleague who proposed mean-proportional constructions examined by Pappus in Book III.

euclid.name: Euclid
euclid.role: Author of the Elements, Data, Porisms & Surface Loci
euclid.summary: Praised by Pappus in Book VII for gentle modesty toward predecessors; author of Elements (generalized in IV.1), Data, the lost three-book Porisms (source of VII.129–139), and the lost two-book Surface Loci (source of VII.238 focus–directrix).

apollonius.name: Apollonius of Perga
apollonius.role: The 'Great Geometer'; author of Conics and six analytical treatises in Book VII
apollonius.summary: Central author of Pappus's Treasury of Analysis (20 of the 33 books) as well as Book II's tetrad arithmetic; expounded across Cutting Off a Ratio/Area, Determinate Section, Tangencies, Inclinations, Plane Loci, and the eight-book Conics.

archimedes.name: Archimedes of Syracuse
archimedes.summary: Revered throughout Books IV, V, and VIII: source of the arbelos ('shoemaker's knife'), spiral quadrature, the 13 semi-regular solids preserved solely in Book V, center-of-gravity mechanics, and the famous saying 'δός μοι ποῦ στῶ καὶ κινῶ τὴν γῆν' (VIII p. 1060).

aristaeus.name: Aristaeus the Elder
aristaeus.role: Author of Five Books of Solid Loci & comparison of the five regular solids
aristaeus.summary: Elder contemporary of Euclid who authored Five Books of Solid Loci (conic sections) in the Treasury of Analysis and investigated the five Platonic polyhedra.

eratosthenes.name: Eratosthenes of Cyrene
eratosthenes.role: Alexandrian polymath & author of On Means (Περὶ μεσοτήτων)
eratosthenes.summary: Invented the mesolabe for two mean proportionals (Book III pp. 56–58) and composed two lost books On Means included at the close of Pappus's 33-book Treasury of Analysis (Book VII p. 636).

nicomedes.name: Nicomedes
nicomedes.role: Discoverer of the conchoid curve for neusis, cube duplication & angle trisection
nicomedes.summary: Introduced the conchoidal curves (κογχοειδεῖς γραμμαί) presented in Synagoge Books III and IV for solving solid neusis problems, duplicating the cube, and trisecting rectilinear angles.

dinostratus.name: Dinostratus
dinostratus.role: Geometer who applied Hippias's quadratrix to circle quadrature
dinostratus.summary: Brother of Menaechmus; demonstrated the rectification and quadrature of the circle by means of the quadratrix (τετραγωνίζουσα), analyzed critically (with Sporus's objection) in Synagoge Book IV.

zenodorus.name: Zenodorus
zenodorus.summary: Established that among isoperimetric n-gons the regular one has greatest area, that a greater-numbered regular polygon exceeds a lesser-numbered one of equal perimeter, and that the circle exceeds every regular polygon—recast and extended by Pappus in Book V.

nicomachus.name: Nicomachus of Gerasa
nicomachus.summary: Classified ten numerical proportions/means in his Introduction to Arithmetic; cited explicitly by Pappus in Book III (p. 68–70) before Pappus's single-semicircle geometric constructions.

heron.name: Hero of Alexandria
heron.role: Alexandrian mechanician, geometer & author of the Mechanics and Baroulkos
heron.summary: Chief authority of Pappus's Book VIII on theoretical and practical mechanics, centers of gravity, the five simple machines, toothed gear-trains, the endless screw, and the Baroulkos weight-hauler.

carpus.name: Carpus of Antioch
carpus.role: Mechanician ('Carpus the Engineer') cited in Book VIII Preface
carpus.summary: Praised alongside Archimedes, Philo, and Hero in Pappus's Book VIII Preface for applying geometry fruitfully to mechanical arts.

proclus.name: Proclus Lycius Diadochus
proclus.role: Neoplatonic scholarch & author of Commentary on Euclid Book I (geometor/proclus)
proclus.summary: Preserves Pappus's famous zero-construction symmetry proof of Elements I.5 (pons asinorum) and complements Book VII of the Synagoge on the epistemology of geometric analysis and porisms.

commandino.name: Federico Commandino
commandino.role: Renaissance humanist mathematician & translator of the 1588 Latin editio princeps
commandino.summary: Translated Books III–VIII of Pappus's Synagoge into Latin with geometric diagrams and commentary (published posthumously at Pesaro in 1588), igniting the seventeenth-century rebirth of analytic and projective geometry.

guldin.name: Paul Guldin, S.J.
guldin.role: Mathematician who independently rediscovered the Centroid Theorem (1635–1641)
guldin.summary: Published the volume-of-revolution centroid rule in his Centrobaryca (1635–1641), unaware or sceptical of the ancient passage already standing in Synagoge VII (Hultsch II p. 682), giving rise to the name Pappus–Guldinus Theorem.

descartes.name: René Descartes
descartes.role: Founder of analytic geometry via the Pappus Locus Problem (1637)
descartes.summary: Made Pappus's Three-, Four-, and n-Line Locus problem (Synagoge VII, Hultsch II pp. 676–680) the centerpiece of his 1637 La Géométrie, proving the power of algebraic coordinates where ancient solid loci had halted.

desargues.name: Girard Desargues
desargues.role: Pioneer of synthetic projective geometry & involution
desargues.summary: Revived Pappus's Book VII projective lemmas on cross-ratio, harmonic division, and involution in his 1639 Brouillon project, inspiring young Blaise Pascal.

pascal.name: Blaise Pascal
pascal.role: Discoverer of the Hexagrammum Mysticum conic theorem (1640)
pascal.summary: At age sixteen generalized Pappus's degenerate two-line Hexagon Theorem (Synagoge VII.138–139) to an arbitrary smooth conic section in his Essai pour les coniques.

steiner.name: Jakob Steiner
steiner.role: Architect of nineteenth-century synthetic projective geometry
steiner.summary: Demonstrated that the six S_3 permutations of Pappus's hexagon generate six Pappus lines concurring three-by-three at two Steiner Star points, and extended Pascal's 60 lines into 20 Steiner points.

hultsch.name: Friedrich Otto Hultsch
hultsch.role: Editor of the authoritative 3-volume critical Greek text of Pappus (1876–1878)
hultsch.summary: Established the definitive Weidmann Greek text, apparatus criticus from Codex Vaticanus Graecus 218, Latin translation, and Index Graecitatis for all surviving books of Pappus's Synagoge.

heath.name: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath.role: Historian of Greek mathematics & commentator on Euclid and Pappus
heath.summary: Authored the comprehensive English mathematical exposition of Pappus's Collection in History of Greek Mathematics Vol. II (1921) and cross-referenced Hultsch's Pappus throughout geometor/euclid.

hilbert.name: David Hilbert
hilbert.role: Author of Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899, geometor/hilbert)
hilbert.summary: Revealed the foundational algebraic role of Pappus's Hexagon Theorem ('Pascal's theorem for two intersecting lines'): in an incidence plane, Pappus's theorem holds if and only if coordinate multiplication is commutative.
